title: Probing crystal-field modulations with magnetic adatoms on the incipient charge-density-wave superconductor $2H$-NbS$_2$
authors: Werner M. J. van Weerdenburg, Margarete Huisinga, Constantin Flommersfeld, Lisa M. Rütten, Katharina J. Franke
abstract: The interplay between multiple quantum phases in layered materials may lead to incipient quantum behavior, where the material's ground state is close to a phase transition and sensitive to local disorder. The transition metal dichalcogenide material $2H$-NbS$_2$ exhibits incipient charge-density-wave behavior along with a well-developed superconducting state, creating a scenario where the local lattice instabilities play a crucial role. Here we present how an individual magnetic atom on $2H$-NbS$_2$ can be applied as a local sensor to reveal hidden crystal-field modulations. By manipulating the adatom across the surface with the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope, we measure variations in the Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) excitation spectra and map the local environment around an intrinsic point defect. We find that while the superconducting state is spatially uniform, the YSR excitation energy strongly depends on the position of the atom. We determine that the main contribution to this effect originates from variations in the local crystal-field environment. These results establish a new approach to investigate crystal-field modulations at the atomic scale and reveal how defects and lattice instabilities shape the atomic landscape of an incipient charge-density-wave material.
summary: This work uses magnetic adatoms on the superconductor 2H-NbS2 as nanoscale sensors to map out subtle electronic variations. By measuring shifts in YSR excitation energies via STM spectroscopy, the authors demonstrate that local crystal-field modulations—rather than changes in the superconducting gap itself—govern the atomic-scale electronic landscape of this incipient CDW material.
main_problem: To use an individual magnetic adatom as a local sensor to reveal hidden crystal-field modulations in the incipient charge-density-wave (CDW) superconductor 2H-NbS2.
main_result: The YSR excitation energy shows strong position-dependent variations, which is attributed primarily to changes in the local crystal-field environment rather than uniform superconducting gap variations or simple LDOS fluctuations.
method: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) spectroscopy was used to map variations in Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) excitation spectra induced by magnetic adatoms across the surface.
model_or_system: The study investigates the layered material 2H-NbS2, which exhibits both superconductivity and incipient CDW behavior. The local electronic structure is probed by depositing single Fe magnetic adatoms onto the superconducting surface.
key_observables: Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) excitation energy ($\epsilon_{YSR}$), superconducting gap measurements, and local density of states (LDOS) variations mapped via $dI/dV$ spectroscopy.
important_parameters: The variation in $\epsilon_{YSR}$ can be significant relative to the inner superconducting gap size; analysis involves distinguishing contributions from crystal-field effects versus LDOS changes.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that variations in YSR energy are sensitive indicators of local structural/crystal-field environment changes, and that these variations can be separated from topographic or simple density fluctuations using Fourier filtering techniques.
figures_summary: Figures show STM images of defects, superconducting gap measurements (uniformity), and detailed maps correlating the measured $\epsilon_{YSR}$ energy with spatial positions across the surface. Analysis figures demonstrate the separation of LDOS variations from topography.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system ($2H$-NbS$_2$) and the sensing mechanism (magnetic adatoms inducing YSR states). It first confirms the uniformity of the superconducting gap, then maps the strong spatial variation in $\epsilon_{YSR}$, attributing this to crystal-field effects after ruling out other sources like LDOS variations.
why_interesting: The technique provides an atomic-scale probe for local structural instabilities (crystal-field modulations) in complex quantum materials near multiple competing phases, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated systems.
